events.title: Battle of Bouvines
events.description: On a Sunday in Flanders, King Philip II of France decisively defeated a coalition of Imperial, English and Flemish forces. The victory crushed the alliance that King John of England had helped assemble against the French crown.
events.significance: The battle effectively ended the Angevin Empire's hold on much of France. It strengthened the French monarchy, and it weakened John's position at home. Within a year he faced rebellious barons and sealed Magna Carta.

events.title: Bank of England receives its royal charter
events.description: A royal charter was granted to the Bank of England. It became the English government's banker, and it raised funds for the government's wars.
events.significance: The Bank grew into one of the world's most influential central banks. It became a model for national banking systems and for the management of public debt.

events.title: Fall of Robespierre
events.description: On 9 Thermidor in the French Revolutionary calendar, the National Convention turned on Maximilien Robespierre. It ordered his arrest, and he was guillotined the next day.
events.significance: His fall ended the Reign of Terror. It marked a turning point in the French Revolution, and the country moved toward the more moderate Directory.

events.title: Bugs Bunny debuts in A Wild Hare
events.description: The animated short A Wild Hare was released. In it a wisecracking rabbit faced off with the hunter Elmer Fudd and uttered his famous question, "What's up, Doc?"
events.significance: The short is widely regarded as the official debut of Bugs Bunny. He became one of the most recognizable cartoon characters in the world.

events.title: Korean War armistice signed
events.description: The United States, China and North Korea signed an armistice agreement that halted fighting in the Korean War. South Korea's president, Syngman Rhee, refused to sign it.
events.significance: The ceasefire ended three years of combat but not the war itself, because no formal peace treaty followed. The Korean Peninsula remains divided along the demilitarized zone.
